before.exam_tip_html: For tropism questions, always describe the mechanism: where auxin is produced, which side it accumulates on, what this does to cell elongation, and the resulting direction of bending. Simply saying ‘the plant grows towards the light’ earns no marks. For gibberellin and ethene questions, link each hormone to a specific commercial application — examiners reward precise examples (seedless grapes, banana ripening rooms, rooting powder) over vague statements about ‘promoting growth’.

For fieldwork questions, examiners want to see: independent variable (what changes along the transect), dependent variable (what is counted), control variables (same-sized quadrat, same observer criteria), how the data are analysed (calculate mean percentage cover, use statistical tests). For 6-mark ‘Describe a Method’ questions on quadrats, mention random number coordinates to eliminate sampling bias. On eutrophication, trace the full chain of events from fertiliser run-off to fish death — partial chains score partial credit.
